content.user_title: Evaluate Job Offers Against Salary Medians
content.value_statement: Job offers combine salary, equity, bonuses, and temporary payments, making comparisons difficult. This skill calculates yearly compensation and compares it with Levels.fyi medians to support negotiation.
actual_capabilities: Extract offer details from a shared letter and ask for missing compensation inputs.
Calculate yearly total compensation using annualized equity and four-year averaging of sign-on and relocation payments.
Calculate first-year compensation using actual first-year vesting and payments, excluding unpromised equity refreshers.
Use Levels.fyi tools to resolve company levels and retrieve company-level medians, market medians, and usual vesting schedules.
Explain compensation gaps, adjacent-level context, currency assumptions, and limitations of all-level market comparisons.
Suggest up to three negotiation points tied to the available compensation figures.
limitations: Live comparisons require Levels.fyi tools and access configured through a separate skill.
Stock options are not valued, and unpromised equity refreshers are excluded.
Free data lacks percentiles, sample sizes, and per-level compensation splits; market medians cover all levels.
Currency conversion can be approximate, and the evaluation is not financial advice.

use_cases.title: Assess a first offer
use_cases.description: Convert a new offer into yearly and first-year totals, then compare available company-level medians.
use_cases.target_user: Job seekers evaluating a first offer

use_cases.title: Prepare a counteroffer
use_cases.description: Identify the compensation gap and develop negotiation points supported by company and market medians.

use_cases.title: Review a retention proposal
use_cases.description: Separate ongoing compensation from temporary payments to assess a retention offer against relevant salary medians.

prompt_templates.title: Start an offer review
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate my job offer against Levels.fyi medians. Ask me for the company, role, level, location, and compensation details you need.

prompt_templates.title: Review an offer letter
prompt_templates.prompt: Read my attached offer letter. Confirm the extracted numbers, ask about missing terms, and calculate yearly and first-year total compensation.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare negotiation points
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my offer with the company median for my level and location. Show adjacent-level context and suggest three negotiation points grounded in available figures.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: use benchmark data for negotiation

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a complex retention offer
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate my retention offer using its uneven RSU vesting, split sign-on payments, relocation, and non-USD salary. Show both totals, currency assumptions, and benchmark limitations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: examine timing and currency differences

output_examples.input: Illustrative offer: USD 150,000 base, USD 200,000 RSUs vesting evenly over four years, USD 15,000 bonus, and USD 40,000 first-year sign-on.
output: Yearly total compensation: USD 225,000, including USD 50,000 annualized equity and USD 10,000 averaged sign-on.
First-year total compensation: USD 255,000, including the full USD 40,000 sign-on payment.
The first-year total is USD 30,000 higher because sign-on is paid immediately rather than averaged across four years.
Company, role, level, and location are needed before selecting a relevant benchmark.

output_examples.input: Illustrative benchmark exercise: yearly offer TC is USD 225,000, company-level median is USD 250,000, and the all-level market median is USD 210,000.
output: The offer is USD 25,000, or 10%, below the supplied company-level median.
It exceeds the supplied all-level market median by USD 15,000, but that median is not a level-matched comparison.
Negotiation point: discuss a stock or sign-on adjustment using the USD 25,000 company-level gap.
These supplied figures illustrate the comparison format and are not verified live salary benchmarks.

best_practices: Confirm the company, level, location, compensation amounts, and payment schedule before evaluating an offer.
Inspect yearly and first-year totals separately, including vesting timing and one-time payments.
Use level-matched company medians when available and label broader market comparisons and approximate currency conversions.
anti_patterns: Treating an all-level market median as a precise benchmark for a specific seniority level.
Counting the entire equity grant as annual income or assuming future refreshers are guaranteed.
Requesting unsupported percentiles or treating the evaluation as financial advice.

faq.question: Which offers can this skill evaluate?
faq.answer: It supports job offers, counteroffers, and retention offers using compensation details you provide or share in a letter.

faq.question: Does it require Levels.fyi access?
faq.answer: Live salary comparisons require Levels.fyi tools. The skill refers to separate setup guidance when those tools are unavailable.

faq.question: Why are yearly and first-year compensation different?
faq.answer: Yearly compensation averages equity and certain one-time payments. First-year compensation uses actual first-year vesting and payments.

faq.question: Can it value stock options or predict refreshers?
faq.answer: No. It mentions stock options without valuing them and excludes equity refreshers that are not promised in the offer.

faq.question: Does free data include salary percentiles?
faq.answer: No. Free data provides medians, without percentiles, sample sizes, or per-level base, stock, and bonus splits.

faq.question: Will it automatically publish my offer details?
faq.answer: No. It asks once whether you want to contribute the offer and delegates only after agreement. The separate contribution workflow is outside this review.
